newsitem.title: JAPAN: Clinton letter to Japan PM cites trade worry - media.
newsitem.headline: Clinton letter to Japan PM cites trade worry - media.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton expressed concern about the Japanese economy and an increase in Tokyo's trade surplus in a letter delivered in early April to Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, Japanese media reported on Wednesday.

Business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun and other media quoted government sources as telling reporters that Clinton also called on Hashimoto to slow down the pace of fiscal reforms in case the economy becomes sluggish and Japan's trade surplus rises.
The letter was dated April 2, just before U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin visited Japan. Rubin urged Japan to guard against a resurgence of its trade surplus.
U.S. officials have expressed concern that a budget squeeze by Japan, including an increase in its consumption tax on April 1, will sap demand in Japan for foreign goods.
Clinton was also quoted by newspapers as expressing concern about Japan's banking system and calling on Japan to carry out further deregulation of its economic system.
Hashimoto is leaving for Washington on Thursday for talks with Clinton on Friday.

The Nihon Keizai also reported that the United States has warned that any rise in Japan's current account surplus over 2.5 percent of its gross domestic product (GDP) would rekindle bilateral trade disputes. Japan's current account surplus stood at 1.4 percent of its GDP in 1996.
The warning was expressed by Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers to Vice Finance Minister for International Affairs Takatoshi Kato when Kato visited Washington on April 7.
